result:
**The plan:** Plan 92 rewrote the writing-skills skill against the Claude Code customization guide. Plan 72's earlier split had left Claude Code facts mixed into `discovery.md` with lint rules and portable advice. A distilled Claude Code file (Decision 10) was still pending. `SKILL.md` was the last STALE file in lint and would soon begin blocking merges. The conformance register also held an open gap and a deviation tied to this rewrite, and the text contained several wrong claims.

**The build:** First, a micro-test kit was set up, and five test arms were registered with fixed pass rules before any run. Next, tests ran on the old text. The RED control passed 10 of 10, so no "critical rules first" instruction was added. The descriptive arm showed agents giving the wrong reason not to fork. Building on those results, a new 64-line `references/claude-code.md` took the version-dependent Claude Code facts. `discovery.md` kept only portable advice, its false claims were corrected, `SKILL.md` gained a pointer, and the register was updated. The new-layout arms then scored 5 of 5 in all 12 cells, and they fixed the forking error, at about $3.43 in total. A 56-row review against the guide led to further fixes and an owner ruling. The citation was restamped at eight sections. Closeout logged the history and the deferred items.

**The project:** Agents on any runtime now read portable guidance, and Claude Code agents follow one pointer to one file that future drift reviews can check. Lint shows no STALE files, three backlog items close, and the register has one fewer gap. The RED record serves as evidence. Five items are deferred.
